Pressman Tri-Ominos - Deluxe Edition Triangular Tiles with Brass Spinners, 5" I’ve always wanted Tri-Ominos because it is a twist on Dominos but uses triangular instead of rectangular tiles and it's lots of fun.

WHAT'S IN THE BOX:
56 triangular tiles
4 plastic tile holders (or racks)
1 instruction sheet

The object of the game is to be the first player to score 400 points with each game consisting of several rounds of play.

For example, with two players, nine tiles are given to each player. The tiles should be face down so that the other player or players don’t see them. Each player adds up the numbers on each of their tiles. If a player has a tile with three of the same numbers on the tile, then the player with the highest combination goes first. For example , a player with three 5’s (which is equal to 15) would go before a player with three 4’s (which is 12) and score the bonus points explained in the instruction card. If no player has a Tri-Omino tile, then the player with the highest numbered tiled goes first but no bonus points would be given.

The idea is for a player to match his or her tile to a tile on the board that has two of the same numbers. They basically get connected the way that it is done with Dominos. The score gets added up for each tile placed. Those that can’t make a match pick from the “well” or remaining face down tiles. Each pick from the well cost the player 5 points from their score. If you can’t match any Tri-Omino in your hand and the well is empty, ten points are deducted from your score and the play continues.

The first player to play all of his Tri-Ominos wins the round and receives a 25-point bonus plus the total points of all the Tri-Ominos left in the other players’ hands. If the game is blocked, then the player with the least amount of tiles wins and gets to add all the points from the left over tiles to their score but there are no bonus points given. This player must also deduct the total number of points that were left in his hand from his score. This method of play gets repeated until a player reaches 400 points to win the game. There are a few other ways to get bonus points in a game as well.

Scoring is done after every play, so from this perspective the game can be tedious. However, it is a lot of fun and for young children, the process of adding up the numbers on the tiles is an education in math. My boyfriend and I really love this game. Playing a full game with two people takes a couple of hours.
text_fidelity_b: Pressman Tri-Ominos - Deluxe Edition Triangular Tiles with Brass Spinners, 5"

text_fidelity_a:
LEGO Star Wars: A New Hope Imperial Star Destroyer 75252 Building Kit (4,784 Pieces) The first thing I noticed about this set was the weight. This is the first LEGO set that I've gotten that I would actually describe as heavy. That's a lot of brick. The box is nice, and contains several smaller boxes. Those boxes have some blueprint art on them, but no useful labeling as to where to begin. You need to open them all anyway, because the unlabeled bags of large parts are mixed in with some of the later bags, despite being needed early on. The bag numbering only goes up to about 20, but there are many bags for each number and the bags have bags in them. The instruction book is huge and spiral bound, with some nice history in the early pages.

The set goes together surprisingly quickly early on, starting with the display base and docking clamps, which the ship is built on, with sections being build and then clipped on. The internal support structure is well engineered and solid. You get a good impression of the overall size and shape of the ship by the time you are done with bag 2.

At first glance, this may look like a tedious grey set where all the parts look the same, but the insides are brightly colored. This is really nice because the parts being built are often rotated between panels, and the colors really help with both finding the parts and orienting with the instructions. When you're done, it also makes it easy to spot anything you missed, because the grey exterior will have rainbow colors there.

One disappointment is the thin area down the sides of the ship. I like them fine individually, but the instructions have you build them identically, so rather than being bilaterally symmetrical, one side looks like it's upside down compared to the other. I understand this saved them some pages, and made construction a little easier, but I would've appreciated a heads up so I could build it mirrored, since I think that would've worked out fine, at least for the greebles on the outside. I may actually take one side apart and redo it, though It's the kind of detail that an observer might not notice because this thing is so big. There are other areas that are more obviously asymmetrical, which is true to the movie, but looks really jarring to me the way they implemented it.

After completing it, I feel like it was designed by two different teams of people. The interior structure is an awesome feat of engineering, and so sturdy you can carry the whole thing by an interior handle, despite its great weight, and they did it with all existing parts. The exterior is about as expected in a Lego set. The transition between the two is weak. Brushing against it risks knocking things off. Sometimes it's just some barely attached pieces on the back, other times something obviously comes apart inside that's going to take some doing to get to and fix. The different sections are often just resting loosely on each other and sometimes look uneven. There is a tiny and comically inadequate clip to hold the four sections of the front in alignment. You may want to think about what you're going to do with it when it's done. It's large, heavy, and oddly shaped. Comes on a nice stand though.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Star Wars: A New Hope Imperial Star Destroyer 75252 Building Kit (4,784 Pieces)

text_fidelity_a:
Klutz Bath and Body Activity Kit Multicolor, 9" Length x 1.75" Width x 9" Height When it comes to making things on our own, my household is a busy place with lots of creativity flowing. When we saw this kit, we could not wait to use it. Finally after waiting due to issues in our house which required a lot of remodeling, we were able to try this out. Let's see how it was..

WHAT IS THIS KIT LIKE?
This kit is one of our favorites. Being those who love color, we enjoyed the beautiful colored box. The box has a very detailed booklet on it which outlines every single project in the box and tells how to do the project. The photography is perfect and easy to read and follow. The layout and writing is perfect for using with children- both younger and older. There is not only an assortment of ingredients all carefully labeled and packaged, but there are little boxes and other decorative containers that you put together to give or display your creations in. I love that the bags are also labeled with what project it is good for and the page number in the booklet which is part of the box, so you won't lose it.

HOW DID OUR CREATIONS TURN OUT?
We had such fun with this. We enjoyed making the Bubble Bath Bon Bons most of all, and they really did work nicely in the tub. We have not done ALL of the projects yet, but the Bon Bons are the favorite so far- especially the marble method of mixing the colors. The little boxes that you put together are really cute and perfect to give as gifts. We also had fun with the lip mask.

ANY DRAWBACKS?
You will have to buy some fresh ingredients for this kit. That means that your treatments will be natural and safe for the face as well as fresh. Strawberry, lemon, avocado, banana, milk, honey, coconut milk, fine sugar or colored sugar, yogurt, and olive oil. Be prepared to have those on hand if you want to do the entire kit. We didn't mind though as we use these things in our home anyway, except for sugar, but I did have some on hand from a sugar scrub we experimented with in the past.

THE BOTTOM LINE
With all of the more unusual ingredients supplied, this kit is great fun to do. My daughter and I had a wonderful time with it. The colors, layout, and packaging are top notch. With the exception of having to provide quite a few fresh ingredients, this is easy and convenient but great fun when you finally do get to have your SPA day!

MY RATING
FIVE STARS! This can be used from young kids who are able to do this with supervision up to older kids- even late teens- who really want to have fun creating a spa day. I can also see using the principles used in this in the future creating a spa day for grandma or others that the kids want to reach out to for a special day.
text_fidelity_b: Klutz Bath and Body Activity Kit Multicolor, 9" Length x 1.75" Width x 9" Height

text_fidelity_a:
Jurassic World Toys , Research Lab Fisher-Price Imaginext toys in general are great toys. Durable, bright colored plastic that often take after popular shows and movies such as Batman and Superman, Power Rangers, or in this case, Jurassic World. These toys have allowed my son's imagination to run wild and be creative as he plays for many hours with these. We often play together, but for the most part he's very happy to play with these on his own for hours at a time. I probably purchased my first Imaginext toy about 3 years ago, Batman and his Batcycle. It has held up to the test of time and a very rough preschooler. My son is now 6 with multiple sets.

Jurassic World has been all the rage in my house this summer because little boys love dinosaurs and that is certainly true of mine! So, take his love for Imaginext toys and mix that with his love for dinos and it's the perfect mashup! The only caveat is that on Amazon I have found the prices to vary greatly from in stores. Toys R Us (R.I.P.) was a great source for Imaginext because they always had the best and lowest price on these. They also had more selections. So, I would caution anyone to first look around Target or Walmart first. I once bought Batgirl and her Batcopter for $30 on Amazon and it was in Toys R Us for $15. I regularly see Imaginext toys in Target selling for $5-10 cheaper than on Amazon.

With the Fisher Price Imaginext Jurassic World Research Lab you get one T-Rex, one scientist, one harpoon, and one claw. There is a "decontamination" chamber for the scientist to get clean to study his subject. Simply turn the powerpad and the blue decontamination spiral gets the scientist ready. There is a powerpad to open and close the cage for the T-Rex. But watch out! The T-Rex might get loose! the lab is not that big. It's smaller than all of the Batcaves I've ever purchased. It's no bigger than any of the Paw Patrol sets I've purchased as well. So, it's east to tuck it away in a corner. All of the pieces, including the T-Rex, we've placed in a plastic show box for organization and storage. Overall, it's a fun play-set that provides hours of entertainment and keeps kids away from screens!
text_fidelity_b: Jurassic World Toys , Research Lab

text_fidelity_a:
Melissa & Doug Deluxe Scissor Skills This is not up to the typical quality of Melissa and Doug products in my opinion. There are 12 mini-projects in this "book"(it's an scruffy bubble envelope with other envelopes inside), and each has some very basic scissor projects. The first one, for instance, has your child cutting in straight lines to create a simple memory game. The second one builds on this, adding some cross-cutting, and so forth.

Each kit is good enough, and the variety is greatly appreciated by the kiddos. In some instances, the instructions needed a little work, while in others, they were perfect. In each case, they're language independent and entirely taught through pictures, which is great for helping the kiddos follow along and do the projects somewhat independently.

There are two pairs of scissors included in this package - a straight pair, and a "scrapbooking" scissor that cuts "teeth" - but these safety scissors are entirely too "safety" for me. The straight one works well enough at first, while the teeth scissors barely worked at all. Their entirely plastic frame wears out with minimal use. There are no metal parts on them, outside of the screws. We had trouble making clean cuts as we approached the middle of the kits, and by the end, we just switched to metal scissors as we were mangling the paper more than doing actual cutting.

The problem with the scissors, as well as the complete lack of a storage solution for these projects as they're in progress is enough for me to rate this kit lower than I normally do. My kit arrived mispacked, so I received two #4 projects, and no #3 project. Good projects can be had here, but bring some of your own materials.
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Deluxe Scissor Skills

Fisher-Price Roar 'n Ride Lion [[VIDEOID:6d6cbfe820d25c4bf20272caa9cdc5e0]] My girlfriend said, "This is the kind of toy that you only get for your worst enemies." I, on the other hand love it! And, kids love it too. The problem with this is that it's a noise-making toy that is very fun and exciting if you're the one controlling it, but kind of annoying if you're not controlling it.

This is a play lion, that comes with suction cups to stick to the side of the car. When you press the lion's belly, then it makes some sounds. When you rattle something, like with the attached rattle, then it does extended music and sound. It's meant to teach kids that if they rattle something, then something else in the environment might react.

One big warning. This ships in Demo mode, where pressing the Lion's tummy works, but the rattle doesn't work. At first I thought it was broken. But, all you have to do is switch this off and then switch it back on, and then both the rattle and pressing the Lion's abdomen will work. And, speaking of switching this off, the switch is hidden on the lion's back, and is super hard to get to. And, it's impossible to change the batteries without ripping the lion's clothes.

Pros:
+Kids love it
+Great for teaching cause and effect
+Makes a lot of noise
+You can stick it on the window

Cons:
-Can be annoying for adults
-On/off switch and batteries are inconveniently located
-Isn't as fun if it's not stuck to a window
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Roar 'n Ride Lion

The Aqua Flash Scorch the Dragon LED Light Up Pool Float is our latest addition to our growing and expanding number of pool accessories.

This pool float is large in size and can hold two young kids with ease. You just inflate, add the lights, and you’re ready to go. They already have plenty of other floats, but none of them have lights like this. During the evening hours, the flashing lights really help to spruce up a party. I did notice that the float does lose air after a few days and we have to re- inflate, but this is common with most floats and isn't an important issue.

Aqua flash Scorch the Dragon LED turned out to be hugely popular with my family and it has been a great addition to our pool. There is no shortage of pool floats on the market, but the difference with this float is the lights. They really add to the float’s appeal and make it an excellent choice as your next pool accessory.

Colored Pencil Set with Case, 7-Inch, Pack of 72 As an artist, I like to keep a variety of pencils on hand for different projects. I decided to test these out in an adult coloring book (with a fairy) and I am actually very impressed. I had low expectations, a lot of people seem to dislike them, but personally I really like them. My husband works at an art and craft store so I have tried a lot of brands and styles. This pack is a great one for starters or to add to your color palette in pencils. Colored pencils can be blended, but it's a lot easier to have a variety of colors to get the shade you want. I spent about 2 hours coloring this page using only pencils from this pack. There are a few colors I would like to have seen, but over all it's still a very diverse pack. There are a lot of lighter and brighter tons than I have in my other pencils.

The pencils themselves have not given me any trouble. The wood is a little lighter than say the Crayola brand ones, but they sharpen fine and as long as you aren't pressing extremely hard the lead does not break. I pressed fairly hard to blend the trees and none of the pencils broke for me. While this was not an art venture, this page was used for me to test the pencils and I am happy with the results. Before I would color on the page, I used a blank page to scribble a little as it can be hard to differentiate some of the colors from the other shades, but I do this anyway so I am sure about the color I want before I get it on the page and accidentally wreck something.

The colors blended fine, I probably should have gone back and finished shading, but as a test page it worked fine. I mixed this pack in with my other pencils so I can choose from any color I could need. When I started out I used the cheap brand from the craft store and these are much higher quality than those ever were.

I wouldn't consider the plastic thing a case though, it's more like a package. Not easy to use. I put my pencils in a storage tote so I could easily go through and choose the one I need. I may end up buying another pack for my mother down the road, she likes to color and basic pencil sets do not have this variety of colors. The price is extremely competitive as well. I paid almost this much for my set of 48 Crayola pencils.

*I RECEIVED THIS PRODUCT (IN ORDER TO TRY IT AND REVIEW) THIS DOES NOT GUARANTEE A GOOD REVIEW OR CHANGE MY OPINION ON THE PRODUCT, I AM HONEST AND UNBIASED, ALL OPINIONS ON IT ARE MY OWN AND BASED ON THE PRODUCT ITSELF. I HAVE TRIED THIS MYSELF AND EVALUATED IT ACCORDINGLY

The Adventures of Robin Hood | A Kosmos Game | Family-Friendly, Cooperative, Role-Player, Story-Driven Game for 2 to 4 Players, Ages 10 and up Several years ago there was a British series about Robin Hood, and my family and I have been hooked ever since seeing that series. This game seemed like a good fit for my family based on our interests, and so far it has been a good addition to family game night. That said, this game tends to be on the easy side and the replayability isn't great if you want a varying experience.

In a nutshell, this is a basic move-around-the-board game at its heart, though it requires cooperation instead of competition and it relies on a story book to further the game along. Some real time and attention to detail went into the design and it shows.

Though the game does not require following a path without turning to the left or right, it does follow a basic flow and the story book is designed to help guide and direct. That said, it essentially is a map of how to get through each step and it does not vary from game to game so once the game has been played the book could potentially slow down a game instead of moving it along at an interesting pace since previous players will know what to do.

This is certainly not a bad game. It's a good family game and is worth running through as a group. However, for those looking for replayability, this one lacks variety.
text_fidelity_b: The Adventures of Robin Hood | A Kosmos Game | Family-Friendly, Cooperative, Role-Player, Story-Driven Game for 2 to 4 Players, Ages 10 and up

Fisher-Price Master Moves Mickey (M3) This is one cool Mickey! In fact, he's so cool his "ice cream doesn't melt"! (one of his cheesy phrases, not mine) Seriously, this has to be one of the coolest toys ever. Not only do both of my boys(16 months and 3 3/4 years) like it, but my husband and I love him, too. Whenever we have visitors, we have to pull this Mickey out, just to show him off. Sad, but true. One day, my 11 year old nephew was over here, and he even commented that this is the "coolest Mickey ever", and his little brother has the original dancing Mickey. I'm not familiar with the other dancing Mickeys, but apparently this one has more features.

My only complaint is the batteries, which really can't be helped with the kind of toy it is. This is more of simply a warning for you than a complaint. This Mickey really sucks the power out of batteries! He takes 6 AA batteries. He does come with a set, but they will wear off REALLY quickly. I would definitely have a high quality set of batteries waiting nearby. When the batteries get low, he will keep moving, but he won't be able to do the really fancy moves, like the handstand, and leg spins. Those are my favorite, so it's disappointing when I don't get to see those. ;)

To make him dance, all you have to do is press his nose. He will only do one set of dance moves and then he will tell you if you want to see more, just press his nose. He turns off pretty quickly. I'm sure this is so he won't use up the batteries even quicker. I like that he's smart, too. When he falls over, he asks for help getting up. When you help him up, he says, Thanks, pal!". There is an on/off switch on the back of his head. I have to make use of this switch when my youngest takes a nap.

Overall, if you don't mind the big investment price and the many batteries he will require, we HIGHLY recommend this Mickey!
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Master Moves Mickey (M3)

Ravensburger Cozy Retreat 500 Piece Large Format Jigsaw Puzzle for Adults - 14967 - Every Piece is Unique, Softclick Technology Means Pieces Fit Together Perfectly I have not done puzzles for years, but recently thought I might like to start again. My first puzzle was 1000 piece and to be honest with you, it was a little frustrating. My eyes aren’t what they used to be and the size of the puzzle was hard for me to work because of the table it was on. I had to stand up a lot to get to the top of the puzzle to work so it just wasn’t relaxing, this time I decided on the 500 piece and I bought this one without realizing the pieces were larger. I am working this on a puzzle mat and it is actually working out the size of 1000 piece puzzle because of the larger pieces. Just be aware of that if you have a smaller place to work your puzzles. So far I am finding this puzzle to be very relaxing and enjoyable there are enough objects in the puzzle so you can get a pretty good idea of where the pieces are going to go in the general area of the puzzle. The pieces are going together very nicely, and there was absolutely no puzzle dust whatsoever in the box.
I would definitely recommend this puzzle especially if you are just getting into puzzles or don’t want one that is very hard. This wouldn’t be considered extremely easy I don’t think but if you are looking for a challenge, I think this one might be a little too casual but for me just getting back into puzzles after years it’s been a very good choice. I’ve been working on it for a few hours today and I have a nice amount completed.

Radio Flyer Pink Rider Trike, Outdoor Toddler Tricycle, Ages 3-5 (Amazon Exclusive) & Pink Helmet, Toddler or Kids Helmet for Ages 2-5 (AC100P) When My Two year old Granddaughter saw this Radio Flyer Red Trike, her eyes lite up,BIG smile on her face,and she was speechless, for a Second!..
It is good looking. Very cute. She loves it.

Although the Plastic tires are a disappointment with out groves in them. Since we live in the mountain, (as they do) on a few acres, the only cement to ride this on is our walkways around the house,
I Then thought she could ride this Radio flyer trike on our long loop Dirt drive-way, but its a bit hilly and the plastic tires are not good for traction on the Dirt, or any light mud going up a hill.
The wheels spin. With out traction its not as fun for her as I thought it would be. We have to push her around in some places.
The good part about the plastic tires are,they will not be popped by the stickers that

and two boxes the Trike came in, It certainly is not damaged.
This comes with very good detailed instruction how to put this together..If my Husband can put this together anyone can.

The little storage compartment in the back is durable plastic, and adorable for girls or boys. My Granddaughter put her dolly in there, with
some other goodies.
The seat will adjusts.

If you live in a area with sidewalks, or have a Large deck the kids will love ridding this Trike, or even on level grass.

I just want to mention, make sure your children have shoes on. I bought a larger Radio flyer for my older grandson (4yr) and he kept
hitting his toes on the cement when peddling . They gave that bike away in less then a month. (his toes where bleeding). They lived in Hawaii, and he was usually bare-foot.

The mech is a good size for kids to be able to grab easily for play, without having to be super careful. Unlike some of Lego’s more fragile sets, this one won’t lose pieces easily.

The mech balances reasonably well, and has enough articulation to be posed, so it could also work as a display piece.

I do wish the back of the mech had more detail and wasn’t quite so flat, but the front is almost cool enough to make up for that. The streamlined look of the armor, and the use of sand green, gold, and even some printed pieces is pretty cool. I also wish the head of the mech had some protection for Lloyd.

I like the detail on the armor of the included minifigs. Quite frankly, they just look cool!

My three-year-old niece was content with using this as is and loves the train so much as a toy that I'll give it 3 stars, but I think many children would prefer the fun of the motorized drill. The "design and drill" is basically some bolts to screw on to hold the covers and the wheels in place. There were several colors of bolts you can choose from to make different "designs."

The engine measures 10 inches long by 6 inches wide by 6 inches tall. The wagon measures 7.5 inches long by 6 inches wide by 3.75 inches tall. The wagon bed is 2 inches deep. The caboose measures 7.5 inches long 6 inches wide and 5 inches tall. Three AAA batteries are needed to power the drill according to the instruction manual, and two AAA batteries are needed for the train engine for the sound and light. The wheels roll smoothly and securely, and it is easy to connect the three sections of the train together, so it is a good toy not just a building activity. There are some extra bolts in case some are lost. The train is sturdy and can withstand the rough treatment of a 3-year-old armed with a plastic hammer.

The instructions aren't that good. If the child has done any other sewing, or has anyone who can help (can be another kid) then this will provide a great deal of practice, which is where this really shines.

There are quite a few projects here. There is a draw string bag, a stuffed cat, a stuffed dog, a stuffed elephant, and a book cover with pencil holder wrapper.

For supplies, it has everything - scissor, tape measure, pins, pin cushion, button, even some extra stuff, like pop poms, that you won't need for any of the projects. There definitely is not even close to enough stuffing. It did not quite fill the cat, which is the first, and smallest, of the stuffed animal projects. You'll want to pick up something like [[ASIN:B000YZ7G44 Fairfield Poly-Fil Premium Polyester Fiber, White, 1 Bag, 12-Ounce]]. Any fiberfill will do, but this is a good one, similar to what is in the kit. While on the topic of stuffing, a double pointed knitting needle, or better http://www.amazon.com/Little-Foot-That-Purple-Thang-/dp/B001ELBCFG/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1464647654&sr=8-1&keywords=purple+thang will help get the stuffing into the tight areas, like the tails. Both the fiberfill and the thang will be useful items in a variety of sewing projects.

For the embroidery floss, it says to cut the skein on one side to make lengths. That works, no issue, but it might be better to make a little yarn butterfly (really simple; instructions are online) so that you can pull the length you need for each section and the leftovers, and there will be plenty, can be used to make friendship bracelets. There is an excess of embroidery floss here.

text_fidelity_a:
Schleich Portable Barn with Accessories The Schleich barn is made of wood and is of extremely high quality except for a problem with the clips and pieces of wood that hold the barn roof together.

The barn opens into two separate unattached halves that slide together at right angles like a puzzle. There are latches on either short side of the barn that can be unlatched to display each half. The barn can be left open or closed. When closed it is easy to carry. A cow, chicken, donkey, lamb, hay bale, basket, red and green vegetables, and a pitch fork and broom are the accessories included. The barn doors on the long side of the barn open in both front and back. The color is vibrant and the farm animals are very realistic.

The only negative I found is that the entire barn is held together with clips that come apart. The clips are not its strongest point. The four clips on either side of the barn roof on mine would not hold up the roof and the boards keep falling off. I tried for over 30 minutes to get two of the clips seated correctly but neither side would snap in place. My boyfriend also looked at this barn and he could not get the clips to seat firmly in place either. He did say, however, that this is a well-made toy. According to the side of the box below the Germany label, it says this is made in Slovakia.

The clips and vegetable pieces that come with the barn can present a choking hazard to a small child. If the child is of that age where items are frequently "tasted," then I recommend adult supervision while the child is playing with this barn. The box indicates that this is not for children under 3 years of age and does state that the small parts present a choking hazard. This is typical of many toys with small parts, however.

Other than this, I got this for my friend's son to play with and he's going to love it. However, he'll have to play with the two roof slats off since they will fall off in its current condition. If the unit I received did not have this problem, I would have rated this 5 stars. Since mine does have this problem, I'm rating it 3. Had I purchased this unit and not received it for review, I would have returned it for a replacement. Since the three other reviewers have not complained about this issue, I suspect it is either a new issue introduced in recent manufacturing design or the unit I received is slightly defective. If there are no other recent reviews that complain about the clips and barn roof, then I would consider this a 5-star toy where I was the one exception. Nevertheless, this defect will not detract from my friend's son enjoyment as young children rarely notice those things.
text_fidelity_b: Schleich Portable Barn with Accessories

text_fidelity_a:
Ben Franklin Toys Electronic Bill & Coin Counter Bank with LCD Screen, One Size This is a really great idea for a children's bank and the top part, the counter, works really well. Unfortunately, there are a number of things here that made it not really work for my family. At least not at this time.

First, with little children in the house, the top buttons get pressed accidentally or on purpose when they are not supposed to and so the count has not been correct for that reason. I almost would've preferred some other method of managing bills and kept this as a coin counter only so that you have the immediate feedback putting something in, seeing the number change, and knowing that it's accurate. This would not be an issue in households only with bigger kids who can control themselves from pushing buttons inappropriately, but definitely made it not workable in my house during these years.

Next, I really hoped that the cool top would have threads so that they could fit on a mason jar of any size, so while the little ones are tiny they can have a little chart, and as they grow older they can have a large jar, but unfortunately it does not work with any size mason jar – the sizing, the threads, and the lip that hangs over are all totally different.

Lastly, and this is my main issue, the cheap, foggy, and unattractive plastic container that holds all of the money is so lightweight and is angled weird so that if there are primarily bills with only a few coins in there, the whole thing gets really top-heavy and wants to tip over. My son primarily gets money through finding change on the ground and through getting dollars or 20s on his birthday or Christmas. So there are a few coins in there, sure, but mostly single bills sent from afar through the mail. Had they made the top interchangeable with Mason jars, this would have been an issue because I just would put the whole thing on nice glass mason jar, probably one of those colored blue, purple, or green ones that they've come out with in recent years. Alas, you're really stuck with just the plastic container that the lid fits on. This limits how long anybody would want to use something like this, because I think most teenagers have slightly better taste than to want some cheap plastic thing of a single specific size sitting in their bedroom.

That said, for a very specific age range and if you don't have smaller children around the house, this could work really well and be a very fun way of having kids learn about saving and making it rewarding.
text_fidelity_b: Ben Franklin Toys Electronic Bill & Coin Counter Bank with LCD Screen, One Size

text_fidelity_a: Manhattan Toy Whoozit Activity Spiral Stroller and Travel Activity Toy I bought this toy thinking it would be good to use on my doorway jumperoo.  The jumperoo has two rings on the two front suspension straps to hang toys on.  But when I got the Whoozit Activity Spiral, it turns out it is very tightly coiled, like a spring; not flexible or bendable.  It is difficult to uncoil it or to stretch it out.  And there is no mechanism to attach it to things.  Although it seems to advertise that you can wrap it around anything, this is completely not true.  There is no wire or anything inside it to attach it with.  If you feed it through a hole, it might stay.  But in the case of my jumperoo, it wouldn't stay hooked on, but just coiled back up and fell off.  So then I tried it on the baby's carseat.  Again, it wouldnt' stay on.  It was too short to wrap a coil from each end around the bars of the car seat, so it would just slide up to the top of the bar as it contracted, or it would fall right off.  IF it were made of something stretchier, or if it had wire inside that would allow you to wrap the ends around something, it might be good. I think the baby would like the little dangling toys on it.  But as it is, it won't attach to anything we have.  And when it is so tightly coiled (as it is all the time unless you're stretching it out yourself) the toys are all jumbled up in the coils and not visible or reachable for baby.  So to me it is a pretty useless toy.

text_fidelity_a:
Playin' Possum This is a great family friendly game that people of all ages can play. The concept is simple in that you need to just try to anticipate what others will play, sort of like rock-paper-scissors. But this game can have multiple players at a time and last until someone either collects enough winning cards (pieces of garbage) or is the last player standing.
The caveats are that you have the ability to "play it safe", which can avoid getting out if someone accuses you of trying to steal on your turn. This can lead to many rounds where nothing happens as someone needs to steal or accuse of stealing for the game to progress. It is also possible to start feeling repetitive after some time as the gameplay does not allow for much variation to keep it interesting. For what it is, it is a fun quick game that doesn't require a lot of setup or learning. But don't expect it to last a long time before people want to do something else instead.
text_fidelity_b: Playin' Possum

text_fidelity_a: Barbie Fashionistas Doll 112 I am a long time Barbie fan. I loved playing with them when I was young, in the 70's. Then in the 90's I collected them. Then in the 2000's I bought them for my little girl. She's graduating from high school next month, but I still love Barbie! I got these for my 5 year old niece to play with when she visits us. I love the variety of body types in this set. I think that's one of the best changes to happen to Barbie ever! This set has 4 different dolls. There's the traditional Barbie that we all love. Then there's the curvy African American doll, a short, petite doll that looks like she could be Hispanic, and a tall , dark hair doll. The thing I love about them (their differences) is also slightly problematic. They all wear different size clothes/shoes. While, that's pretty normal in the real world, it's more difficult in the Barbie world. Some of the dolls could probably get away with sharing clothes, but curvy doll is out of luck. I hope to see more curvy doll size clothes in the future! And if you are planning to gift this, be aware that they don't come in the typical pink Barbie box. text_fidelity_a:
City Fire Station Building Blocks Set W/ Fire Truck, Fire Rescue Helicopter, Drone & Fire Engine Toys, Fire Command Center Playset, Firefighters Roleplay Toy Gifts for Kids Boys Girls Ages 6+ (744PCS) It's fake LEGO. It may pretend it isn't, but it is,
As well as being fake LEGO it has one other claim to fame.
It is very disappointing.
When companies copy (not be inspired by. I am all for being inspired! this is copying) because of patents, they cannot copy the construct of the bricks. So they end up with bricks that do not push together well, giving models less resilience to being knocked over, picked up or even played with.
Except for the tile pieces. They stick like they were coated in gorilla glue! You may need power tools to get them apart.

Aside from the poor quality of the bricks, what else can be said? Nothing good, sadly. The set designs are primitive. The vehicles are not all on the same scale. Some will not hold the minifigs.
The accessories are another disappointment. Ugly, hard for the minifigs to hold.

If you have a nephew or niece who loves LEGO, and you simply cannot stand this family member, you have found the perfect gift.

Otherwise, keep looking. You will pay more for LEGO, and it is worth every cent!
text_fidelity_b: City Fire Station Building Blocks Set W/ Fire Truck, Fire Rescue Helicopter, Drone & Fire Engine Toys, Fire Command Center Playset, Firefighters Roleplay Toy Gifts for Kids Boys Girls Ages 6+ (744PCS)

text_fidelity_a:
Marbotic - Sensory Kit for iPad - Wooden Interactive Lowercase Letters and Numbers for Learning to Read & Maths -Ages from 2 to 5- Used in Kindergartens I generally don't prefer electronic learning, but these are pretty cool. The Smart Letters each have three rubber feet that are spaced differently, and the tablet recognizes the letter when you gently place it on the tablet screen. It took about 10 minutes to download all 6 free apps (3 for letters, 3 for numbers) and to set up the quick profile. The apps are simple to use and well designed. Next is a summary of the 3 letter apps:

Bla Bla Box: spell out words and hear them read back to you
Alphamonster: choose a letter to hear the sound the letter makes and see a picture of a word beginning with that letter. See a picture of an item and identify what letter the item starts with. Hear a sound of a letter and identify the letter. See a cursive lowercase letter and identity the matching wooden uppercase letter. (In the settings you can pick which letters will appear throughout these challenges. The default is the entire alphabet but you can pick just a few if your child needs to focus on certain letters)
Vocabubble: game 1- pick any letter and as you repeatedly place the letter on the tablet, 8 different pictures of items beginning with that letter will fall down the screen. Game 2 - choose two letters, then pictures of items beginning with those two letters will fall down the screen and you tap the picture with the right letter in order for it to disappear. (This was a fun game my niece and nephew enjoyed playing together as they each held a letter. However, some pictures seemed too hard or random for a 5 year old, such as an Orca for the letter O... kids will think it's a Whale... or a Totem Pole or Quaill, etc)

My five year old niece and nephew enjoyed testing these for me and were definitely interested in the games. I'm excited to start my daughter with it when she turns three and I can see the number apps extending the usefulness of the product as she gets older. Four stars, not five, only because they do seem a bit pricey and also because the accent on the American English setting we tried out is a bit odd at times.
text_fidelity_b: Marbotic - Sensory Kit for iPad - Wooden Interactive Lowercase Letters and Numbers for Learning to Read & Maths -Ages from 2 to 5- Used in Kindergartens

text_fidelity_a:
Akedo Ultimate Arcade Warriors Ultimate Battle Arena Action Figure, 3 Pieces THE GOOD:
--------------
* Perfectly priced toy for the quality you're getting.
* Collectible.
* Like Rock-Em Sockem, but with electronics, and the figures will split when getting knocked out.
* This version come with an arena, but you can fight without it if you wish.
* Two warriors included to get you started.

THE BAD:
-----------
* Nothing I can think of. The price is just right for what you're getting. I don't recall an actual arcade game in the past called Akedo. It seems this toy is simply inspired by all the classic arcade fighting games such as Street Fighter, Fatal Fury, Tekken, etc. It will keep your children occupied for awhile and away from tablets.

One more thing, the two default figures that's already installed in the arena have clear bands wrapped around them. We saw the vertical bands on their bodies and cut them off. But when we battled, we still couldn't split each other. My son realize there are more tiny bands in the neck that needs to be cut. So if you're playing for awhile, and you can't knock anybody out, check to see if rubber bands are still holding their bodies tight. You can manually check... you are free of bands when you can pop their heads back and split their bodies. If you can't do that, it probably means there are some bands you still need to cut off.

5-Stars!

text_fidelity_a:
IDO3D Pen and Ink Up to 25 Projects Print System - 5 pens What a great creative art toy. You can do literally anything with this and takes your sketches off the paper and into three dimensions. I am amazed at the ways the kids put this into practice, and it kept them engrossed for hours with only a couple squabbles over people hogging this color or that. I'll get more into what we did below. But first, What you get and How this works.

This product is a hardening gel that can be squeezed into shapes using plastic forms. There are several forms that come with the kit, a flat sheet of plastic and a couple rounded forms for creating spherical shapes. The flat clear piece is great for tracing images so even young kids can achieve the shapes they desire. Also, we used it to make other curves to help flesh out animal shapes, but that proved a little more difficult.

Once you have drawn your shapes with one of the gel pens, you can use the UV flashlight to harden the pieces to make them retain the shapes you want. Then you can peel them off the plastic forms or sheet and cement elements together into three dimensional structures. The possibilities are endless and only limited by creativity. Our kids started out by tracing the provided dinosaurs and moved on to tracing other dinos from various books until they had a small forest of dinos and trees.

Warnings and caveats: I'm a little leery of the chemically nature of this toy. There are warnings to avoid skin contact in light. This put me a little on edge and I wanted to supervise our 8 through 14 year olds to make sure it was not getting on skin or other stuff. Also, this does take a bit of artistic ability. It can be as free form as you want it to be, but we did have some frustration when younger kids could not recreate the stuff the older kids were building. But for the most part it was very conducive to creativity.

Also, the end products are a little sticky. So they don't seem like you can play with your creations, but you can make wonderful visual art. We have a nice little dino diorama on our book shelf now and the kids seem pretty proud of it. The inks are also a little messy, so make sure your in a cleanable area.

Personally, I think this is one of the most wonderfully novel and creative ideas I've seen in a while. I will be picking up some for the kids on my Christmas list, and look forward to refilling our supply.
text_fidelity_b: IDO3D Pen and Ink Up to 25 Projects Print System - 5 pens
